the ids it was given alongside the one it created. Same outcome, same
shape — an integrator handling one does not need a second reader for the
other.

it is data the caller already sent, and re-emitting it would spread
personal and business information across another response body and another
log line for no gain.

and that is where the current review status is read from:

* ``card_acquiring_id`` -> ``GET /v1/platform/card-processing/{id}``
* ``kyb_id`` -> ``GET /v1/platform/card-processing/kybs/{kyb_id}``

MorePayoutRequest.title: MorePayoutRequest
MorePayoutRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /tenant/international/payouts/process``.

**Sender is server-managed.** API consumers never need to supply sender /
business-identity fields. Finogates resolves the sender block from the
SUA-configured platform defaults (``Tenant.meta['uniteller_sender_defaults']``)
and injects it into the outbound provider call. This is part of the
Finogates orchestration contract — provider-specific mandatory fields are
enriched server-side, never required from the customer.

The endpoint accepts two shapes:

* **Canonical (preferred)** — ``product_id`` + ``payee_payment_method_id``.
  Routes through ``ensure_tenant_product_entitled`` → ``select_provider``
  → ``reserve_funds`` → ``ensure_payment_method_binding`` → provider call
  → ``move_escrow_to_clearing`` / ``release_escrow``. Recipient and bank
  info are loaded from the saved ``PaymentMethod``.
* **Legacy (deprecated)** — inline ``beneficiary`` + ``bankInfo``.
  Bypasses the entitlement / ledger / binding pipeline. New integrations
  MUST use the canonical shape; the legacy shape is retained only to
  avoid breaking the integration that just shipped.

Exactly one of the two shapes must be present.

Internal/advanced fields (not part of the public surface, retained for
backward compatibility):

* ``sender_id`` — explicitly select a saved ``InternationalSender`` row
  instead of falling back to the platform defaults. Tenant-managed by SUA;
  most integrators leave this unset.
* ``sender`` — inline override of the sender block. **Deprecated and
  ignored by default**: server-side enrichment runs whenever the
  enrichment dispatcher returns a populated block, so this field is
  effectively only honored when the platform has no defaults configured.

OAuthCallbackCreate.title: OAuthCallbackCreate
OAuthCallbackCreate.description:
Posted by the Finogate FE landing page after the end-user returns.

``code`` and ``state`` are read verbatim from the callback URL the user
landed on. The BE verifies the signed ``state``, then:

* If ``code`` is present (verified flow via ``/login/oauth/authorize``)
  → exchange the code at ``POST /oauth/token`` for an access_token +
  card_id, fetch + persist that card.
* If ``code`` is absent (receive-only flow which does NOT emit an auth
  code) → look up the user's existing link from the signed state, mint an
  access_token via the partner-identity flow, list the user's cards,
  persist any new ones.

``state`` is therefore the load-bearing identifier — it carries the
tenant + user + mode + return_url attribution and is HMAC-verified by
:func:`oauth_state.decode_state`. ``code``, when present, is supplied by
the processor and is single-use at their end.

and settles via webhook.

payment_type.description: Optional movement classification. ``transfer`` moves your own money (e.g. a bank deposit into your own wallet); ``send`` pays another party (e.g. a wallet → bank payout). When omitted the server derives it from the source and destination. When provided it is validated against them and rejected on mismatch.

idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key
idempotency_key.description: Unique key to ensure idempotent payment creation.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata to attach to the payment.

destination_wallet_id.title: Destination Wallet Id
destination_wallet_id.description: Destination wallet UUID to credit — another user's wallet (or your master wallet) on the same platform. The server validates tenant ownership and ``currency`` and resolves the owner from it.

from_hold.title: From Hold
from_hold.description: Draw this transfer from the source wallet's frozen (held) funds instead of its available balance. The held balance must cover the amount plus any payer-borne fee, or the request is rejected with ``insufficient_held_funds``. Omit for a normal transfer from available balance.

PaymentWalletToWalletCreate.title: PaymentWalletToWalletCreate
PaymentWalletToWalletCreate.description:
Move funds to another wallet on your platform (``intent_type=transfer``).

A wallet-to-wallet transfer is **user-to-user**: it moves money from the
source wallet (``wallet_id``) to another user's wallet
(``destination_wallet_id``) on the same platform. Both wallets must
belong to your platform — cross-platform transfers are not allowed. The
master wallet may be on either side. No KYC/KYB is required to transfer
between wallets.

PayoutCountryCreate.title: PayoutCountryCreate
PayoutCountryCreate.description: Payload to create a new Payout country entry.

PayoutCountryEnablementUpdate.title: PayoutCountryEnablementUpdate
PayoutCountryEnablementUpdate.description:
Turn Finogate's support for a destination on or off, in one mode.

The mode is taken from the request (``X-Finogate-Mode`` / host policy) and
is never a body field: it must be the same mode the operator is looking at
in the console, not one they can disagree with in a payload.

PayoutCountryUpdate.title: PayoutCountryUpdate
PayoutCountryUpdate.description:
Payload to update a Payout country entry. All fields optional.

``is_enabled`` is deliberately absent — it is an authorization boundary and
is mode-scoped, so it has exactly one writer: ``POST
/admin/payout-countries/{id}/enablement``. Accepting it here too would give
the same state two writers with different audit trails.

PendingApplicationCancelRequest.title: PendingApplicationCancelRequest
PendingApplicationCancelRequest.description: Optional submitter-supplied reason for withdrawing an application.

merchant_id.title: Merchant Id
merchant_id.description: Gateway merchant account identifier (NMI MID internally).

processor_id.title: Processor Id
processor_id.description: Processor identifier (NMI processor_id internally). Optional — leave blank/omit to use the default processor configured on the MID.

security_key.title: Security Key
security_key.description: Gateway security key. Encrypted at rest.

nmi_webhook_secret.title: Nmi Webhook Secret
nmi_webhook_secret.description: Per-MID HMAC signing secret for inbound NMI webhooks. Encrypted at rest.

external_bank.title: External Bank
external_bank.description: True if the merchant's card-acquiring funds settle to their own external bank (pass-through). False (default) uses a Finogate virtual bank visible in the wallet.

PendingApplicationCardAcquiringApprove.title: PendingApplicationCardAcquiringApprove
PendingApplicationCardAcquiringApprove.description:
Card-acquiring approval payload.

Captured by the SUA admin when they one-click-approve a
card-acquiring application from the pending-applications queue.
The field names are operator-facing (``merchant_id`` /
``processor_id``) — the route maps them to the internal NMI columns
(``nmi_merchant_mid`` / ``nmi_processor_id``) inside the service.

Public-API exposure: none. This schema is admin-realm only.

provider_message_id.title: Provider Message Id
provider_message_id.description: Provider messaging-service identifier for the enrollment.

PendingApplicationMessagingServiceApprov.title: PendingApplicationMessagingServiceApprove
PendingApplicationMessagingServiceApprov.description:
Per-phone-number messaging-service link approval.

The admin supplies the provider's messaging-service identifier, captured
out-of-band in the provider console. Saved onto the
``PhoneNumberMessagingService`` link so outbound SMS from that number route
through the registered service. Format-agnostic — no provider validation.

phone_sid.title: Phone Sid
phone_sid.description: Twilio IncomingPhoneNumber SID (PN...) for the purchased number.

phone_number.title: Phone Number
phone_number.description: E.164 phone number actually purchased. Overrides the value supplied at request time.

iso_country.title: Iso Country
iso_country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code of the purchased number. Overrides the value supplied at request time.

PendingApplicationPhoneNumberApprove.title: PendingApplicationPhoneNumberApprove
PendingApplicationPhoneNumberApprove.description:
Phone-number request approval.

Carries the Twilio account credentials (nested under ``credentials``)
plus the purchased Twilio number identifiers. ``phone_number`` and
``iso_country`` overwrite whatever the tenant supplied at request
time so the ``UserPhoneNumber`` row reflects the number actually
bought in Twilio.

PersonaInquiryResponse.title: PersonaInquiryResponse
PersonaInquiryResponse.description:
Result of starting (or resuming) a Persona identity check.

Two ways to continue the check may be returned — use whichever is set,
preferring ``inquiry_url`` when present:

- ``inquiry_url`` — a hosted page the user should be sent to (browser
  redirect, new tab, QR code, or iframe).
- ``session_token`` — a token for loading Persona's JavaScript SDK
  directly, together with ``inquiry_id``.

PersonaKycRequest.title: PersonaKycRequest
PersonaKycRequest.description: Request to create a Persona KYC inquiry.

email.title: Email
email.description: Platform contact email. Must match the configured PHONE_CALL_ONLINE_EMAIL secret (compared case-insensitively).

password.title: Password
password.description: Must match the configured PHONE_CALL_ONLINE_PASSWORD secret.

PhoneCallOnlineLoginRequest.title: PhoneCallOnlineLoginRequest
PhoneCallOnlineLoginRequest.description:
Shared-credential login for the phone-call-online integration.

The configured ``PHONE_CALL_ONLINE_EMAIL`` and ``PHONE_CALL_ONLINE_PASSWORD``
secrets are exchanged for a platform token identical to the one issued by
``POST /v1/platform/auth/token``. Both values must match; the password
alone will not mint a token for a different platform email.

PhoneNumberAssignCreate.description: Assign a phone number to a user.

PlatformBankAccountCreate.description: Add a bank account as a payment method.

PlatformCardProcessingMidRead.description: Narrow platform read for one card-processing MID/config bundle.

product.title: Product
product.description: Public product identifier. Always ``card_acquiring`` for rows returned by this surface.

kyb_id.title: Kyb Id
kyb_id.description: Public ``id`` of the KYB (``compliance_checks``) row this application was made against.

merchant_info_submitted_at.title: Merchant Info Submitted At
merchant_info_submitted_at.description: When the merchant_info packet (supporting documents + volume figures) was last submitted. Null when never submitted — lets a detail view render the state without a second round-trip.

PlatformCardProcessingRead.title: PlatformCardProcessingRead
PlatformCardProcessingRead.description:
Platform-realm projection of CardAcquiringRead.

Wire-identical to CardAcquiringRead: ``product`` is ``"card_acquiring"``
on every realm. This class used to override it to ``"card_processing"``,
so the platform and tenant card-processing surfaces returned a different
product string from the admin one for the same row; that split is gone and
one row now reads the same everywhere.

Only the ``/card-processing`` URLs and the ``card_processing_*`` error
codes keep the newer vocabulary — the path is the public route name and
the codes are rewritten on the platform boundary in ``app/main.py``;
neither is affected by this field.

Kept as a distinct name because it is what the platform and tenant routes
and :class:`CardProcessingMerchantRead` are written against, and because
the two may diverge again.

payment_method_id.title: Payment Method Id
payment_method_id.description: Public id of the saved card to charge.

card_acquiring_id.title: Card Acquiring Id
card_acquiring_id.description: Public id of the card-acquiring merchant to deposit into. Optional — when omitted the tenant's first approved (oldest created) card-acquiring account is used. When supplied it is always honoured; there is no fallback, and a card vaulted under a different account is refused.

payer_user_id.title: Payer User Id
payer_user_id.description: Public id of the payer (cardholder) user being charged.

destination_wallet_id.title: Destination Wallet Id
destination_wallet_id.description: Public id of the exact wallet to credit. Optional — when omitted the funds land in the card-acquiring account owner's primary wallet for the currency. The wallet must belong to this tenant and its currency must match ``currency``; it does not have to be a primary wallet. Not accepted when the card-acquiring account settles to an external bank account.

idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key
idempotency_key.description: Caller-chosen unique key; a replay returns the same record.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Optional caller metadata stored on the record.

PlatformCardToMerchantCreate.title: PlatformCardToMerchantCreate
PlatformCardToMerchantCreate.description:
Request body for ``POST /v1/platform/payments/card-to-merchant``.

The card is identified by ``payment_method_id`` (a card already vaulted
for a user under the tenant). ``card_acquiring_id`` selects the NMI
merchant (MID) the funds deposit into; it must match the merchant the
card was vaulted under (vault tokens are MID-namespaced). Omit it to use
the tenant's first approved card-acquiring account.

download_url.title: Download Url
download_url.description: Short-lived link to a document already sent. Absent on unanswered items, and on a stored file that could not be signed.

PlatformDocumentItemRead.title: PlatformDocumentItemRead
PlatformDocumentItemRead.description: One thing being asked for, and the answer if it has been sent.

subject_scope.title: Subject Scope
subject_scope.description: ``user`` when the check is about one of your users, ``tenant`` when it is about your own platform.

kyc_record_id.title: Kyc Record Id
kyc_record_id.description: The identity check this belongs to. Present on ``kyc`` and ``mkyc`` checks; the same value the ``user_kyc.*`` webhooks send.

kyb_record_id.title: Kyb Record Id
kyb_record_id.description: The business check this belongs to. Present on ``kyb`` checks; the same value the ``user_kyb.*`` webhooks send.

PlatformDocumentRequestListRead.title: PlatformDocumentRequestListRead
PlatformDocumentRequestListRead.description: The document requests on one verification check.

outstanding_required.title: Outstanding Required
outstanding_required.description: Required items still unanswered. Zero once the round is done.

note.title: Note
note.description: Message from the reviewer who raised the request.

cancel_reason.title: Cancel Reason
cancel_reason.description: Why the reviewer withdrew a ``cancelled`` round.

PlatformDocumentRequestRead.title: PlatformDocumentRequestRead
PlatformDocumentRequestRead.description:
One round of questions against a verification check.

The check's id is not repeated here — it is on the enclosing object, and
one round can only belong to one check.

fee_code.title: Fee Code
fee_code.description: The fee line to price, e.g. ``ach.push`` or ``card.acquiring``.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: The payment amount (major units) to price the fee against.

PlatformFeeQuoteRequest.title: PlatformFeeQuoteRequest
PlatformFeeQuoteRequest.description:
Quote one fee line for an amount on the public platform API.

The platform is taken from your credentials — you supply only the line and
the amount. The quote runs the same engine real charges use, so it reflects
your active **override** when one is set, otherwise the **global** default.

PlatformKycRead.title: PlatformKycRead
PlatformKycRead.description: Platform's own KYC check, trimmed for the self-service KYC detail page.

PlatformKycSyncRead.title: PlatformKycSyncRead
PlatformKycSyncRead.description: The current state of a user's identity (KYC) check after a refresh.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: Owner user UUID.

last4.title: Last4
last4.description: Last 4 digits of the card number.

card_transfer_aft_enabled.title: Card Transfer Aft Enabled
card_transfer_aft_enabled.description: True when this card is registered for card-to-account (money-in) transfers on the platform. Always false for non-card methods.

card_transfer_oct_enabled.title: Card Transfer Oct Enabled
card_transfer_oct_enabled.description: True when this card is registered for account-to-card (money-out) transfers on the platform. Always false for non-card methods.

billing_address.title: Billing Address
billing_address.description: Card billing address (line1, city, state, postal_code, country).

routing_last4.title: Routing Last4
routing_last4.description: Last 4 digits of the routing number.

routing_number.title: Routing Number
routing_number.description: Full ACH routing number (9 digits) of the bank account.

account_holder_zip.title: Account Holder Zip
account_holder_zip.description: Account holder ZIP or postal code.

rail_code.title: Rail Code
rail_code.description: Primary rail this instrument was registered for, if any.

PlatformPaymentMethodRead.title: PlatformPaymentMethodRead
PlatformPaymentMethodRead.description:
Payment method representation for the platform API.

Sensitive data (full PAN, full account number) is never returned —
only masked values (``last4``, ``account_mask``).

tenant_id.description: Tenant UUID to generate the billing preview for.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the preview.

PlatformProductionEligibilityRead.title: PlatformProductionEligibilityRead
PlatformProductionEligibilityRead.description: Whether this platform account is cleared to handle real, live money.

PlatformUserComplianceRead.description: A user's full identity (KYC) and business (KYB) verification details.

PlatformUserComplianceSummary.title: PlatformUserComplianceSummary
PlatformUserComplianceSummary.description: A short summary of one user's identity (KYC) and business (KYB) checks.

first_name.title: First Name
first_name.description: User's given name. Required for an individual (`is_business_user` false); ignored for a business.

last_name.title: Last Name
last_name.description: User's family name. Required for an individual; ignored for a business.

name.title: Name
name.description: Deprecated combined full name for an individual. Send `first_name` and `last_name` instead; when only `name` is provided it is split into first/last automatically and must carry both.

is_business_user.title: Is Business User
is_business_user.description: Set to true when this user is a business/organization rather than an individual. When true, send `business_name` and omit first/last name. This is fixed at creation and cannot be changed later.

business_name.title: Business Name
business_name.description: Organization name. Required when `is_business_user` is true; leave empty for an individual.

email.title: Email
email.description: User's email address. Must be unique within the platform and RFC 5321 compliant.

PlatformUserCreate.title: PlatformUserCreate
PlatformUserCreate.description: Create a new end user on the platform.

PlatformUserDetailsUpdate.title: PlatformUserDetailsUpdate
PlatformUserDetailsUpdate.description:
Update a user's name on the platform.

Every field is optional; send only what you want to change. Only the name is
touched — email, status, wallets, and the individual/business type are left
untouched (the type is fixed at creation). For an individual, update
`first_name`/`last_name`; for a business, update `business_name`. If the user
has already passed identity verification, a changed name must match the
verified name on file (case-insensitive) or the request is rejected.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: Unique user identifier (UUID).

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name — the business name for a business, otherwise the combined given + family name.

is_business_user.title: Is Business User
is_business_user.description: Whether this user is a business/organization rather than an individual.

business_name.title: Business Name
business_name.description: Organization name — populated for a business, null for an individual.

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: Whether the user account is active.

kyc_status.title: Kyc Status
kyc_status.description: This user's own KYC status — a ``ComplianceCheckStatus`` code (1=pending, 2=in_review, 3=approved, 4=rejected). For the tenant's master user this is the platform's tenant-scope status; for an end user it is their individual verification. Null if no KYC check exists yet.

kyb_status.title: Kyb Status
kyb_status.description: This user's own KYB status — a ``ComplianceCheckStatus`` code (1=pending, 2=in_review, 3=approved, 4=rejected). For the tenant's master user this is the platform's governing (onboarding-linked) KYB; for an end user it is their individual business verification. Null if no KYB check exists yet.

PlatformUserRead.title: PlatformUserRead
PlatformUserRead.description:
User representation returned by the platform API.

``hashed_password``, or ``tenant_internal_id``.

PlatformUserVerificationRead.title: PlatformUserVerificationRead
PlatformUserVerificationRead.description:
The identity verification (KYC) details on file for one user.

Combines the latest identity check (status, decline reason, email,
verification inquiry id) with the personal information captured during
verification (name, date of birth, address, ID document images, etc.).

user_id.description: End user the virtual bank account is opened for.

PlatformVirtualBankAccountCreate.title: PlatformVirtualBankAccountCreate
PlatformVirtualBankAccountCreate.description:
Public platform request shape for ``POST /platform/virtual-bank-accounts``.

Field aliases accept both the spec-style camelCase (``userID``) and
the canonical snake_case so integrators can use whichever they
prefer; documentation should standardise on snake_case.

user_id.description: End-user UUID owning the wallet.

make_primary.title: Make Primary
make_primary.description: If true, atomically demotes the existing primary wallet in (user, currency) and promotes this new one. The user's first wallet in a currency is always primary regardless of this flag.

PlatformWalletCreate.title: PlatformWalletCreate
PlatformWalletCreate.description:
Platform-realm (OAuth2 client) wallet creation payload.

Integrators provision wallets for their end users via this surface.
Unlike the tenant-realm payload, ``user_id`` is always required — the
OAuth2 client acts on behalf of the platform itself, not a logged-in
user.

events.title: Events
events.description: Individual event types to subscribe to. An empty list subscribes to all events.

most-recent failures.

ProdKycRedeemRequest.description: Payload posted to the production-host redeem endpoint.

rail_code.description: Rail code the product belongs to.

activated.description: True when this platform has the product enabled.

platform_product_status.title: Platform Product Status
platform_product_status.description: This platform's enablement status for the product, if any.

ProductCatalogItemRead.title: ProductCatalogItemRead
ProductCatalogItemRead.description: A single platform-visible product in the onboarding catalog.

enabled.description: True to enforce the product gate, False to stop enforcing.

ProductGateUpdate.title: ProductGateUpdate
ProductGateUpdate.description: Turn a feature's product gate on (enforce) or off (break-glass).

ProviderBalanceRefreshCreate.title: ProviderBalanceRefreshCreate
ProviderBalanceRefreshCreate.description: Re-poll one provider account's balance right now.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: Compute and report, write nothing. Run this first: it tells you exactly how many rows would be priced and to what total, so the figure can be checked against the invoice BEFORE it is committed.

ProviderFeeBackfillCreate.title: ProviderFeeBackfillCreate
ProviderFeeBackfillCreate.description:
Re-price movements already in the ledger against the cards in force.

Fees are stamped at write time, so a card added today leaves every existing
row at ``provider_fee_minor = NULL``. Without this the first invoice after
configuring a provider always reconciles as ``disputed``.

amount_billed_minor.title: Amount Billed Minor
amount_billed_minor.description: What they billed. OMIT IT to track a period whose bill has not arrived yet — the row stays `pending` with no variance. It is never defaulted to 0: that would mean 'they billed nothing', and every open period would reconcile as `disputed` by exactly our own accrual.

lines.title: Lines
lines.description: Their bill's lines. Only valid once the bill has arrived.

ProviderInvoiceCreate.title: ProviderInvoiceCreate
ProviderInvoiceCreate.description:
What a provider ACTUALLY billed us for a period.

Entered by hand — no provider we integrate exposes a billing API.

``lines`` are optional. Supplying them is what turns "the bill is $12 off"
into "physical_check is $12 off", which is the difference between suspecting
an over-charge and being able to dispute it. If given, they MUST sum to
``amount_billed_minor`` — both are transcribed from the same PDF, so
cross-checking them catches the typo that would otherwise be blamed on a
service.

ProviderInvoiceLineCreate.title: ProviderInvoiceLineCreate
ProviderInvoiceLineCreate.description:
One line transcribed from the provider's bill.

``service`` should match a key we record movements under (``digital_check``,
``ach_pull``, …) so it can be compared against what we accrued. Anything else
is accepted as a **custom line** — a setup fee, an overage, a credit — and is
reported as fully unexplained variance rather than dropped.

ProviderInvoicePaidUpdate.title: ProviderInvoicePaidUpdate
ProviderInvoicePaidUpdate.description:
Mark a provider's bill paid, or un-mark it.

Deliberately not a ``status`` value — see ``ProviderInvoiceRead.status``.

account_ref.title: Account Ref
account_ref.description: The provider's own id: the Checkbook wallet id, 'default' for UniTeller, the Twilio Account SID.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: 'float' = customer money in transit (a diff means money is MISSING). 'vendor_credit' = our prepaid opex (a diff means an unrecorded top-up). Defaults from the provider.

seed_from_provider.title: Seed From Provider
seed_from_provider.description: Poll the provider's live balance now and seed the opening balance in the same call. Equivalent to registering then seeding.

ProviderLedgerAccountCreate.title: ProviderLedgerAccountCreate
ProviderLedgerAccountCreate.description:
Register an account we hold at a provider.

Accounts are normally born inside the recorder on the first movement, so a
movement is never dropped. This route is for registering one **before** any
traffic — which is what makes a clean genesis possible (see
``ProviderLedgerAccountSeedCreate``).

provider_balance_minor.title: Provider Balance Minor
provider_balance_minor.description: Override the polled balance. Leave null and the provider is asked for its own balance — which is the point. Only supply this for a provider whose balance we cannot read.

ProviderLedgerAccountSeedCreate.title: ProviderLedgerAccountSeedCreate
ProviderLedgerAccountSeedCreate.description: Seed an account's genesis — the balance that predates the ledger.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: Which way the money moved. On an ``opening_balance`` there is no movement to have a direction, so send ``in``.

amount_minor.title: Amount Minor
amount_minor.description:
Minor units (cents), always positive — ``direction`` carries the sign.

**On ``opening_balance`` this is not a movement**: it is the provider's CURRENT balance, exactly as shown on their dashboard. The server posts the delta that lands our running balance on that figure, so an account that already recorded movements (every VBA and Check-Mail wallet does — they are discovered by the webhook that creates them) seeds to the truth instead of double-counting them.

memo.title: Memo
memo.description: Shown on the row in the grid.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why. Recorded on the audit log, not on the row.

ProviderLedgerEntryCreate.title: ProviderLedgerEntryCreate
ProviderLedgerEntryCreate.description:
A manual ledger entry posted by an operator.

``opening_balance`` is the load-bearing one: it seeds the account's genesis
from the provider's live balance and flips the account active. Until it is
posted, the account publishes no diff.

Append-only — there is no update or delete. A correction is a new
``adjustment`` row.

operation.title: Operation
operation.description: Only ``top_up`` and ``adjustment`` are editable. ``opening_balance`` is the genesis — correct it with an appended ``adjustment`` instead.

ProviderLedgerEntryUpdate.title: ProviderLedgerEntryUpdate
ProviderLedgerEntryUpdate.description:
Edit a MANUAL ``top_up`` / ``adjustment`` row, then recompute balances.

This is the one deliberate departure from the ledger's append-only rule, and
it is confined to the narrowest safe case: a row an operator authored **by
hand** and may simply have got wrong. A machine-recorded movement is never
editable — its correction is a real provider event.

``opening_balance`` is **not** editable either: it is the ledger's genesis,
set once from the provider's live balance, and its stored amount is a derived
delta rather than a movement. Correct it by posting an ``adjustment`` (which
is appended, so the history of what was believed and when survives).

Editing ``amount_minor`` / ``direction`` re-sequences ``running_balance_minor``
(and any persisted ``balance_diff_minor``) for this row **and every later row
in the account**, so the write is guarded with ``update`` and fully audited.

The account, currency and ``effective_at`` are fixed — an edit corrects a
row in place, it does not move it between accounts or re-order the statement.

UniTeller prices per corridor — a Mexico bank transfer is $0.90 and a China one is $5.50 — so its cards are country-specific. An unconfigured country resolves to no card and reports its cost as `unknown`; it NEVER falls back to another country's price.

delivery_method.description: How the money is delivered, in UniTeller's own numeric vocabulary (the same one its branch catalogue carries): 1 = BANK TRANSFER, 2 = CASH PICKUP, 3 = WALLET (the rate sheet's 'Mobile Money'). NOT interchangeable — Uganda is $1.80 by bank transfer and $2.00 by cash-out. NULL = one price for every method in this country.

deducted_from_balance.title: Deducted From Balance
deducted_from_balance.description:
Does the provider take this fee OUT OF our float?

When true, the recorder appends a companion `provider_fee` movement that actually moves the running balance. When false, the fee is only a column on the movement it priced (Checkbook = false: invoiced monthly, verified).

It records a BELIEF, and a wrong one is self-revealing: the balance drifts monotonically at (txn_count x fee), which the drift checker attributes back to this flag.

**Rejected for Twilio.** Twilio reports its own prices and its usage charges are already ingested as balance-moving rows, so setting this would debit the float twice for the same money.

Declare what a provider charges US.

Necessary, not a convenience: most providers never return a fee. Checkbook's
check object has no fee field at all (verified against their live sandbox),
so configuration is the only possible route.

deducted_from_balance.title: Deducted From Balance
deducted_from_balance.description: True for UniTeller: it takes its fee out of the prefunded FBO, so the fee is a real balance-moving row, not just a cost column.

effective_from.title: Effective From

ProviderRateCardImportCreate.title: ProviderRateCardImportCreate
ProviderRateCardImportCreate.description:
Load a provider's whole rate sheet in one go.

UniTeller's sheet is ~66 countries x up to 3 delivery methods. Nobody types
that through a dialog, and a hand-typed corridor is a wrong price waiting to
happen — which is worse than no price, because it misreports margin AND feeds
drift attribution, where an inflated expected fee can explain away missing
money.

Defaults to ``dry_run``: resolves every ISO code against the payout-country
catalogue, prices each row through the real fee engine, and reports the lot —
so the mapping is reviewed BEFORE anything is written.

actions.title: Actions
actions.description: Major-unit decimal STRINGS, fed verbatim to the shared fee calculator: {'flat_fee': '1.80'} | {'percent_fee': '1.60'} | both, for a sheet row like USA's `0.25% + 1.80 USD`.

ProviderRateCardPreviewCreate.title: ProviderRateCardPreviewCreate

Price a DRAFT rate card — one that has not been saved yet.

Exists so the SUA never has to reimplement the fee calculator to answer "what
would this form charge?". There must be exactly one implementation of money
maths (``fees_engine_service.calculate_fee_from_actions``); a second one in
another language will drift, and the day it does an operator is shown a price
the system does not actually charge.

topScore.title: Topscore
topScore.description: Highest match score among the hits (0.0–1.0), or null if none. DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — a name-similarity score, not a risk score. Do not build thresholds on it: a true watchlist entry scores 0.8122 on name alone while an innocent common name scores 0.7513; the score is not comparable between subjects screened with different amounts of identity data; and it moves as the watchlists refresh (the same entry scored 0.8762 and then 0.9025 two days later, unchanged software). Lists reload every 12h. Act on 'decision', which is a stable contract.

confirmWith.title: Confirmwith
confirmWith.description: The ONE piece of identity data that would most improve this result — the strongest field you have not already sent. At most one entry, so send it and POST a new check; if that still hits, the next check asks for the next field, and nothing already in hand is ever asked for twice. Populated only when there is something to resolve ('review' or 'blocked'); empty on 'clear', and empty on 'unavailable' because nothing was screened. Empty on a hit means the check is already as strong as this API can make it and the remaining question needs a human.
